```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(reach.rate)
library(data.table)
```

**Audience:** technical. You are checking that an installation of the package
behaves as its tests say it should, reviewing what those tests cover, or adding a
case of your own.

# Why synthetic stations

A real station never tells you the true rating, so a fit to real gaugings can be
checked for consistency but never for correctness. A synthetic station can. Each
case below generates gaugings from a rating the package knows, with scatter, fits
them with the guided workflow, and asks whether the answer comes back.

# Read this first

**These ten cases were written by the package's author.** They are not the cases
of any external specification: the brief that asked for a reference suite never
supplied its list, so these are my own choices, covering the situations I think
matter most. They are a starting point for a reviewer to extend.

**Passing them is necessary, not sufficient.** Ten tidy synthetic stations say
nothing about a real one. They catch a package that has broken, not a rating that
is wrong.

**The tests are about envelopes, not coefficients.** A case does not demand that
`C`, `a` and `n` come back to three decimals. Several triples describe nearly the
same curve, and a platform's arithmetic can move them in the last places. What
matters is the discharge a user would read off. So each case states an
**envelope**, the largest relative error allowed between the fitted curve and the
truth across the gauged range. Each envelope is set with room to spare: no case
uses more than half of it.

# The cases

```{r cases}
cases <- reference_cases()
knitr::kable(cases[, .(Case = id, `What it tests` = purpose, `What it does not` = not_tested)])
```

A case passes when four things hold. The fitted curve stays inside its envelope.
The optimiser converged and the rating is valid. Any parameter the case checks
(the zero-flow stage, an exponent) is recovered. And the assessment raises the one
check the case was built to trigger, for the five that have one.

```{r designed}
knitr::kable(cases[!is.na(designed_check), .(Case = id, `Envelope` = envelope, `Check it must raise` = designed_check)])
```

# Running them

```{r run}
res <- check_reference_cases()
knitr::kable(res[, .(Case = id, `Largest error` = round(max_rel_error, 3), Envelope = envelope,
                     Converged = converged, Valid = valid, `Check raised` = check_raised, Passed = passed)])
```

`check_reference_cases()` is exported so that the same run can be made on any
machine the package is installed on, such as one it is about to be used on. It
takes a few seconds and changes nothing: it leaves your random seed as it found
it and moves no rating's lifecycle.

```{r summary}
cat(sprintf("%d of %d cases passed.\n", sum(res$passed), nrow(res)))
```

# Looking at one case

```{r one}
case <- reference_case("two_limbs")
fit <- do.call(fit_rating, c(list(case$data, quiet = TRUE), case$fit_args))
stage <- c(0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0)
data.table(stage = stage,
           truth = round(case$truth(stage), 2),
           fitted = round(apply_rating(fit, stage)$discharge, 2),
           relative_error = round(apply_rating(fit, stage)$discharge / case$truth(stage) - 1, 3))
```

Each case is `reference_case(id)`: its `data`, identical on every call, the
`truth` as a function of stage, the arguments it is fitted with, and the range and
envelope it is judged over.

# What a failure would mean

A failing case is a finding about the installation, not a verdict on any rating.
Which part failed says where to look:

| Fails | Look at |
|---|---|
| The envelope | The fitting code or a dependency: the optimiser, `minpack.lm`, a platform's arithmetic |
| Converged or valid | The same, and `vignette("mathematical_contract")` for what valid means |
| A parameter | Bounds on the exponent, or the starting values |
| The designed check | The assessment's limits: `vignette("thresholds")` |
| The channel-shift contrast | Age weighting: `vignette("recency_weighting_guide")` |

# Adding a case

A case is one entry in the package's list of specifications: a title, a seed, a
true rating, a way to generate the data, an envelope, and the check it should
raise if any. The package's tests loop over every case, so a new one is tested
without further work. Choose the envelope by running the case and leaving at least
double the error you see, then say plainly in `not_tested` what the case cannot
show.
